key_insight: Machine learning potentials connect localized molecular rotations to orientational defects that persist as collective relaxation fades during AESO photopolymerization.
engineering_relevance: Estimating rotational barriers can help interpret dielectric monitoring of curing in bio-based polymer networks.
method: Measure dielectric permittivity at 500–5000 Hz during intermittent UV curing of AESO:VDM.
Analyze relaxation dynamics using sliding-window Shannon entropy and Grassberger–Procaccia correlation integrals.
Compare MACE-OFF23 relaxed dihedral scans of five AESO rotational modes with DFT reference profiles.
evidence_signal: MACE reproduces all five DFT profile shapes with Pearson r = 0.95–0.98; an Arrhenius estimate places acrylate rotations closest to the dielectric measurement window.
watch_item: MACE underestimates rotational barriers by 3–20%, and fragment-level scans do not fully represent constraints in the curing network.
paper_title: Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
